description: A single-panel table (no lettered sub-panels; one rendered table image) comparing calculated and experimentally observed constituent phases of two Fe-Mn-Al-C steels after annealing at different temperatures for 100 h. The table is split into two halves: left half headed "Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C", right half headed "Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C". Each half is subdivided into a "Calculated" block and an "Experimental" block, and each block has the column headers "Phases" and "T (°C)". Rows list phase sequences versus temperature: for Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C the calculation gives γ (>780), γ→γ+α (780–730), γ→γ+α+κ (730–610), γ→γ+α+κ+M7C3 (610–540) and γ→α+κ+M23C6 (540), while experiment gives γ (>825), γ→γ+α (800), γ→γ+α+κ (750–650), γ→γ+α+κ+M23C6 (625) and γ→α+κ+M23C6 (600–550). For Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C the calculation gives γ (>750), γ→γ+α (750–745), γ→γ+α+κ (745–495), γ→γ+α+κ+M23C6 (495–420) and γ→α+κ+M23C6 (420); experiment gives γ (>850), γ→γ+κ (850–775), γ→γ+α+κ (775–600), γ→γ+α+κ+M23C6 (600) and γ→γ+α+κ (550). The table demonstrates that FactSage-calculated phase boundaries lie systematically below the experimentally observed ones and that M7C3 is predicted in one steel but M23C6 is found experimentally.

observations.observation: The figure is a single table comparing Calculated versus Experimental constituent phases for two Fe-Mn-Al-C steels, with columns headed 'Phases' and 'T (°C)' in each of the four blocks.
The two steel compositions printed as table headers are 'Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C' and 'Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C'.
For Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C the calculated single-phase γ field extends to T >780 °C, whereas experimentally γ is retained to T >825 °C.

For Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C the calculated γ field extends to T >750 °C while experimentally γ persists to T >850 °C; the two temperatures are printed as separate column entries (calculated >750 vs experimental >850).
The calculation for Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C predicts the carbide M7C3 in the range 610–540 °C, but the corresponding experimental row lists M23C6 at 625 °C instead.
Both calculated and experimental columns for Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C contain the κ-carbide (γ + α + κ) and M23C6 fields.
Experimentally, Fe-18Mn-7Al-0.85C shows a γ → γ + κ transition at 850–775 °C that is absent from its calculated column.

Experimental transition temperatures in both steels are printed at higher values than the corresponding calculated ones (e.g. γ→γ+α+κ at 750–650 °C experimental vs 730–610 °C calculated for Fe-13.5Mn-6.3Al-0.78C).
The table reports phase stabilities after annealing at different temperatures for 100 h for the two Fe-Mn-Al-C steels.
The calculated columns in the table are FactSage calculations, cited as references [108,109].
The figure compares the constituent phases of the two steels with thermodynamic calculations, i.e. it assesses how well FactSage reproduces the observed phase fields.
